Harness plugin that reports the time you spend coding with AI to WakaTime as `ai coding` heartbeats.
# dsh-plugin-wakatime
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Host plugin that reports the time you spend **coding with AI** inside DSH t
o WakaTime, as `category: "ai coding"` heartbeats, so it shows up in your **AI Coding** stats next t
o everything else you track.
It does not fake per-file keystroke heartbeats. It answers one question — was this stretch of time s
pent working on this project with an AI pair? — and it does so in the background, without blocking t
he host. Since v0.2 it also ships a **Usage** page inside DSH.
## Features
- **Project-aware** — `entity` is the session's working directory, `project` is its folder name, so

AI time is broken down per project in WakaTime.
- **AI-shaped heartbeats** — every beat carries the

DSH session id, input/output token deltas, and how many characters you typed.
- **Follows real DSH a
ctivity** — user messages, assistant replies, tool calls, and turn boundaries all count; a 15 s keep

alive covers long turns, and an idle timeout stops the clock when you walk away.
- **Nothing lost of
fline** — 429/5xx/network failures land in a local queue (atomic writes, 500 beats max) and are repl

ayed with backoff; a 401 stops sending instead of hammering the API.
- **Built-in Usage page** — a s
idebar entry with today / this week / all-time time, a 7-day chart, top projects, token and keystrok

e counts, plus the WakaTime-side view.
- **Harmless without config** — no `api_key` means one warnin
g in the log and an inert plugin; DSH starts normally.
## Install
The bundle needs its own dependency first: `install_bundle` symlinks a local directory and does **no
t** install what the bundle depends on.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then install the repository root as a bundle from DSH's Plugin Manager:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**Restart DSH** after installing or upgrading — the Host code lives in the server process, so refres
hing the page is not enough. Remove it with `remove_bundle` (package name `dsh-plugin-wakatime`).
Prerequisite: an `api_key` under `[settings]` in `~/.wakatime.cfg` — the same file your other WakaTi
me clients already use. Its `proxy`, `hostname`, and `debug` values are reused.
## Configuration
Config lives on the plugin's row (`config` in `cordis.patch.yml`, or the form in Settings). Preceden
ce: plugin `config` > `~/.wakatime.cfg` > built-in defaults.
| Key | Default | Purpose |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch. |
| `minIntervalSeconds` | `120` | Minimum gap between heartbe

ats, all sessions combined. |
| `idleTimeoutMinutes` | `15` | Gap that ends the current timing stret

ch. |
| `entityType` | `'file'` | `file` reports the project path; `app` reports `DeepSeek Harness`.

|
| `includeSubagentSessions` | `false` | Count subagent sessions separately (off: the same wall-cl

ock time is not counted twice). |
| `category` | `'ai coding'` | WakaTime activity category. |
| `ap

iKey` | empty | Overrides the `api_key` from `~/.wakatime.cfg`. |
| `debug` | `false` | Verbose diag
nostics in the log file. |
An empty string means "fall back", not "set it empty". The remaining keys — `apiUrl`, `proxy`, `host
name`, `language`, `userAgent`, `projectFromCwd` — and the exact semantics of all of them are in doc
uage`, `userAgent`, `projectFromCwd` — and the exact semantics of all of them are in docs/design.md.
## Usage
v0.2 adds a **Usage** page: a sidebar entry sitting next to Plugins, Automation tasks and Context in
sights. It is fed by the Host route `GET /wakatime/usage.json` (`Cache-Control: no-store`), so every
thing shown is real data from this machine.
| Block | Shows |

| Local time | today (large), this week, all-time |
| Today's volume | input / output tokens, charac

ters typed, sessions, heartbeats |
| Last 7 days | inline SVG bar chart, one bar per day |
| Project

s | top 5 by tracked time |
| WakaTime | whether `api_key` is configured, hostname, today's remote A
I Coding time, pending queue size, last send, last error |
Page copy is bilingual and follows DSH's language setting (`en` / `zh`), and the page is drawn with
the host's theme variables, so it matches light and dark. The remote figure is derived from your hea
rtbeats (`GET /users/current/heartbeats?date=…`, AI Coding categories only, 60 s cache); if that one
request fails, only that block reports an error and the local stats keep working. A refresh button
re-fetches the JSON.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
- Triggers: `user/message`, `assistant/message` (with `usage`), `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `turn/st

art`, `turn/end`; running turns stay alive thanks to a 15 s tick.
- Auth: `Authorization: Basic base
64(api_key)` against the WakaTime API v1. Each beat also feeds a local per-day store (`usage.json`,

30 days) that backs the Usage page.
- Diagnostics: `<DSH_HOME>/cache/wakatime-dsh/wakatime.log` (or
`~/.dsh/cache/…` when `DSH_HOME` is unset). The offline queue and state live in the same directory.
## Privacy
Sent to WakaTime: project working-directory path, project name, DSH session id, input/output token c
ounts, characters typed, timestamps, plus `language` and `hostname` when configured.
**Never sent**: code, prompt text, model output, file contents, terminal output. The plugin works on
event metadata, never on the text itself. The usage store stays on your disk.
## Development
